about: Standard-level assessment of the estate against the SEBI Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework (CSCRF). 'entity' rows are obligations of the regulated entity that software cannot discharge. SEBI categories: MII, Qualified RE, Mid-size, Small-size, Self-certification.

source.title: SEBI Cybersecurity and Cyber Resilience Framework (CSCRF) for SEBI Regulated Entities
source.issued: Circular SEBI/HO/ITD-1/ITD_CSC_EXT/P/CIR/2024/113, 20 Aug 2024, read with the clarifications of 31 Dec 2024 (CIR/2024/184), 30 Apr 2025 (CIR/2025/60) and 28 Aug 2025 (CIR/2025/119) and SEBI's June 2025 FAQs
source.caveat: CSCRF is a circular, not a Master Direction. Standards (e.g. PR.AA.S1) are grouped where the guideline block groups them. Applicability is taken from the guideline tables in the circular; later circulars and the entity's category assignment can change it. Obtain the entity's category and check for SEBI circulars issued after 28 Aug 2025 before relying on this.

items.title: Cybersecurity roles and responsibilities (own staff, third-party staff, privileged users) defined and aligned
items.note: Organisational.

items.title: Understand and comply with IT Act, DPDP Act 2023, SEBI/GoI circulars; audits and inspections by SEBI and its agencies; forensic auditor for root cause
items.note: PII redaction targets Indian identifiers (Aadhaar with Verhoeff, PAN, UPI) before text reaches a model and a DPDP mapping exists; consent, erasure, breach notice and inspection access are the entity's processes.
items.next: Add a DPDP data-principal-request helper (export/erase a user's chat data across the stores) with a journey.

items.title: CISO (MII, QRE: reports directly to MD & CEO) / Designated Officer (others); time-bound incident reporting channel to CISO
items.note: Appointment and reporting line are the entity's. The SOC case feed is the time-bound channel SecuRAX can supply.

items.title: Separate cybersecurity budget head; adequate resources
items.note: Entity's budget.

items.title: Employee due diligence, screening, onboarding training, exit procedures; NDAs and due diligence of third-party providers
items.note: HR and procurement.

items.title: Board-approved cybersecurity and cyber-resilience policy covering CSCRF (deviations justified) and the listed sub-policies (asset, patch, vulnerability, VAPT, audit, monitoring, configuration, change, SSDLC, authentication, authorisation, segmentation, encryption, PII, etc.)
items.note: Board-approved policy documents are the entity's. The compliance maps and docs 04/27 are inputs, not the policy.

items.title: Regulatory Data and IT & Cybersecurity Data made accessible to SEBI on request, including data held by external parties (in the agreement)
items.note: The evidence pack and audit lines can be produced on demand; external-party clauses are contractual.
items.next: Define the 'SEBI request' export (scope, format, 48 h target) as a documented command.

items.title: PDCA documentation, compliance-management programme, IT Committee for REs with periodic reviews placed before the Board; review of incidents
items.note: Governance forums are the entity's. `ccsp`, `comply` and `fitness` supply the review inputs.

items.title: NCIIPC CII principles where identified as CII; adopt ISO 27001/27002 practices
items.note: Entity decision; NCIIPC applicability is notified, not self-declared.

items.title: Cyber Capability Index (CCI, Annexure-K): MII third-party assessed, Qualified RE self-assessed, half-yearly; dashboard integrated with log aggregator available at audit/inspection
items.note: CCI (Annexure-K, ~25 pages of indicators with weights) is not computed; the nearest thing is the CCSP and compliance coverage maps.
items.next: Implement CCI scoring as a questionnaire-plus-evidence tool that reads the same evidence references as the compliance maps, with a dashboard export.

items.title: Cyber risk-management framework (ISO 27005 as guidance): risk appetite, controls, monitoring; metrics MTTD/MTTR/MTTC, false positives/negatives, phishing-test rate, EOL-software counts; risk-based transaction monitoring
items.note: The purple loop reports prevented/logged/alerted and the SOC counts cases, but MTTD/MTTR/MTTC and false-positive rates are not computed and there is no EOL/asset metric.
items.next: Compute MTTD/MTTR/MTTC and FP/FN rates from SOC cases in the evidence pack.

items.title: Comprehensive scenario-based testing of cyber risks (attack scenarios per business model)
items.note: Scenario-based testing exists for AI-channel attacks (purple loop) and infrastructure failures (game days); Annexure-E scenarios for exchanges are not modelled.
items.next: Add ransomware-on-backups, credential-theft and third-party-outage scenarios.

items.title: Third-party service providers must adhere to CSCRF; cyber-audit certificates obtained; responsibility stays with the RE; periodic reports name providers of critical activities
items.note: Contractual and assurance obligations of the entity.

items.title: SBOM for existing and new critical software/SaaS; SBOM contents (licence, supplier, transitive dependencies, hashes...)
items.note: CI generates a CycloneDX SBOM for this repository's images and `vet` records licence, pins and tree hashes for third-party content; SBOMs of the entity's other vendors must be obtained from them.
items.next: Publish the SBOM as a release asset and include it in the evidence pack.

items.title: Identify third-party providers posing concentration risk; independent audit; validate resilience
items.note: Provider failover (local → Gemini → Groq → OpenRouter...) avoids a single AI-provider dependency; no register of concentration risk.
items.next: Provider register with concentration flags and exit plans.

items.title: Critical systems identified, classified and approved by the Board; inventory of hardware, software, digital assets, APIs, cloud assets, data flows; updates within 3 working days; criticality assessment (threat modelling, VA)
items.note: Estate components, endpoints and models are inventoried from the genome and registry; the entity's wider inventory, Board approval and the 3-day update discipline are not automated.
items.next: Emit a machine-readable inventory (components, images, ports, data flows) and diff it against the previous run to prove the 3-day rule.

items.title: Up-to-date network architecture diagram (wired and wireless)
items.note: Architecture diagrams exist for the estate; not generated from live state.
items.next: Generate the diagram from the compose/Kubernetes definitions so it cannot go stale.

items.title: Configuration-management database; all IT assets in an ITSM tool; cybersecurity in product life cycles
items.note: No CMDB/ITSM integration.
items.next: Export the inventory in a CMDB-importable format.

items.title: Half-yearly (MII) / yearly (QRE, mid-size) risk assessment including post-quantum risk; quantifiable cyber risk score
items.note: AI-SPM and the registry assess the AI estate; no risk score and no post-quantum assessment.
items.next: Compute a transparent risk score from findings × asset criticality and list quantum-vulnerable algorithms in use.

items.title: Dark-web monitoring and take-down; anti-phishing/anti-rogue-app services; SOPs for CERT-In/NCIIPC advisories with timeframes; process IOC/IOA/malware alerts; onboard to CERT-In intelligence platform; MIIs on NCCC
items.note: The offline CISA KEV and MITRE ATT&CK snapshots enrich SOC cases and `scan`; the MISP organ can hold indicators. No dark-web/brand monitoring, no CERT-In advisory ingestion or SOP.
items.next: Ingest CERT-In advisories (RSS/CSV the entity receives) into the SOC enrichment with a response-time clock.

items.title: Monitor for phishing sites impersonating the RE's domains and report to CSIRT-Fin/CERT-In; risk-based authentication (device, location, network)
items.note: No look-alike-domain monitoring and no authentication at all on the gateway (see PR.AA).
items.next: Look-alike domain watcher (certificate-transparency + DNS permutations) feeding SOC cases; risk-based login belongs to the IdP.

items.title: Least-privilege, purpose- and time-bound access; periodic review of access, delegated access and unused tokens; unique logged access to critical systems retained ≥2 years (6 months online); lock-out after failed attempts; dormant-account review; leaver de-provisioning; MFA for internet-facing critical systems and all remote/VPN/webmail access
items.note: No authentication, accounts, lock-out, dormant-account review or MFA at the gateway or its consoles (the principal is a hash of the caller string or IP). Log retention beyond what the shipper keeps is not enforced.
items.next: Identity-aware gateway: OIDC/JWT validation, roles, per-subject rate limits, lock-out, session logging, MFA via IdP; retention policy enforced and tested (2 years, 6 months hot).

items.title: Anti-malware/IPS on servers, baseline configuration standards with enforcement checks, secured LAN/Wi-Fi, SMTP limits
items.note: The gateway manifest and Kyverno policies enforce non-root, read-only root filesystem and dropped capabilities, and Trivy scans images in CI; configuration baselines are code in git. Endpoint anti-malware and LAN/Wi-Fi controls are the entity's.
items.next: Add a CIS-benchmark check (kube-bench/docker-bench) to CI and record the baseline.

items.title: PIM process/solution; strong password controls; internet access policy; supervise and restrict privileged users, forbid privileged users from reading logs of their own activity
items.note: No privileged-access management; no separation between who runs the gateway and who can read its audit log.
items.next: Admin role separate from auditor role; audit-log store append-only for the admin role.

items.title: Network segmentation/isolation; WAF, proxy, IPS; web/e-mail filtering; whitelisted ACLs; DNS filtering and DNSSEC; critical-server management only via intranet; SPF/DMARC/DKIM; authorised device inventory
items.note: Tenant cells ship default-deny NetworkPolicies and quotas; the gateway applies an outbound link allow-list on model output. WAF, mail, DNS and device controls are the entity's perimeter.
items.next: Provide a reference egress policy for the gateway (only the router) and test that direct egress is blocked.

items.title: Isolate and secure perimeter and connectivity of servers running algorithmic trading
items.note: No algorithmic-trading applications in the estate.

items.title: Zero-trust: critical systems deny-by-default; delegated access and unused tokens reviewed and cleaned quarterly
items.note: Default-deny network policy per tenant; user/token review and identity-based zero trust are not implemented.
items.next: Short-lived tokens issued by the IdP and a quarterly token-review report.

items.title: Password complexity, first-login change, history, validity; credentials stored with strong hashing; generic IDs removed
items.note: The gateway stores no passwords; where Keycloak/Open WebUI hold users, their policies apply and have not been tested here.

items.title: Identify all log sources and collect them (system, application, network, database, security, audit); retention per law; monitor all logs
items.note: Gateway decisions are logged and monitored; other organs are not uniformly collected. Retention is declared (≥180 days) but not enforced or tested.
items.next: Log inventory per organ, central collection, retention enforcement test.

items.title: Physical access restricted and supervised; screening; critical-equipment room perimeter, guards, CCTV, card access; remote-support service governance, RDP with MFA and whitelisted IPs; environmental monitoring
items.note: Premises and remote-support contracts. For the on-prem burrow, the room is yours.

items.title: Data-disposal and retention policy; secure disposal of media (wipe, degauss, crypto-shred, destroy)
items.note: `prune` deletes stage data after a typed confirmation and keeps nothing; media sanitisation is not performed or recorded.
items.next: Record disposal in the evidence pack; encrypt volumes so deletion of keys crypto-shreds them.

items.title: EPP/EDR/XDR, NG-IPS, PowerShell and local admin off by default, AD review for backdoors and service-account compromise, penetration testing of AD abuse, removable media policy; (MII) secure domain controllers
items.note: The Wazuh organ gives endpoint/host detection (optional); the range (GOAD) lets you rehearse AD attacks and review controls. Production AD hygiene is the entity's.
items.next: Ship the Sigma/Atomic-test pairs for the AD abuse techniques the range reproduces.

items.title: API security (rate limiting, authentication/authorisation, OWASP API Top 10, whitelist connections); mobile-application security (root detection, anti-tamper, device binding...); SOPs for open-source application security and Generative-AI security (MII, QRE)
items.note: Gateway: rate limiting, request-size limits, prompt-injection and PII rails, output link allow-list, tool-call inspection; mapped to OWASP LLM Top 10 and ATLAS and exercised by the purple loop. No API authentication (see PR.AA.S1-S3); no mobile apps.
items.next: Add authentication (above), then a written GenAI-security SOP generated from the rails and the purple-loop results.

items.title: Cybersecurity awareness and training for employees (phishing, social engineering) and outsourced staff; programmes kept current
items.note: People programme.

items.title: Customer-facing grievance, fraud-reporting and investor-education features in mobile/web apps
items.note: No investor-facing applications in the estate.

items.title: Encryption in motion, at rest and in use with strong algorithms; FDE + file-based encryption; encryption of data in cloud (Annexure-J)
items.note: Cloud data volumes use KMS encryption; provider traffic is TLS; local loopback traffic, local volumes and backups are unencrypted; no data-in-use protection.
items.next: Encrypt backups; document LUKS/FDE for the burrow; TLS between internal components; test with a TLS policy scan.

items.title: Data-loss prevention; prevent unauthorised access, copying, transmission of contractual/fiduciary data; authorised storage devices only
items.note: On the AI channel the gateway redacts PII and secrets before text reaches a model, blocks exfiltration patterns in model output, and the purple loop proves the redaction and the alert. Scope: data passing through the gateway only — not e-mail, endpoints or removable media.

items.title: Application security for customer-facing internet applications (IBTs, portals, back office); Annexure-G measures
items.note: No customer-facing trading or back-office applications.

items.title: Real-time capacity monitoring with alerts; comply with SEBI capacity-planning circulars
items.note: Resource budgets, elasticity and a watchdog are tested; no real-time capacity alerting to a SOC and no SEBI capacity-planning report.
items.next: Export capacity metrics and thresholds to the SOC feed.

items.title: Regulatory Data kept within India in readable form; global SOC / SaaS exemption for IT & Cybersecurity Data only with annual IT-Committee and Board approval and 48-hour availability to SEBI/CERT-In
items.note: Prompts go to Gemini/Groq/OpenRouter and other cloud rungs of the router when keys are present; PII redaction reduces but does not remove regulatory data. There is no rule that 'regulatory data never leaves India'. The local-only profile keeps everything local, but nothing enforces its use for classified data.
items.next: Classification-aware routing: tag requests (by tenant/endpoint/detected data class); regulatory data may only use local or India-region providers, enforced and logged in the gateway; journey proves a classified prompt never reaches a foreign provider.

items.title: Classify data per SEBI/GoI standards (IT Act, DPDP)
items.note: The gateway classifies PII types it can detect; no enterprise data-classification scheme.
items.next: Map detected classes to the entity's classification labels and carry the label in the audit line.

items.title: Data protection, backup and recovery; admin rights off by default on workstations; no sensitive data in client-side storage; renew certificates; control macros; data-migration policy
items.note: Backup and restore are proven; endpoint admin rights, macros and certificate renewal are the entity's; backups are unencrypted.
items.next: Encrypt and checksum backups.

items.title: Separate production and non-production; SIT; OWASP/SANS-25 vulnerabilities addressed; DevSecOps
items.note: Everything is built and tested in a throwaway sandbox clone with real containers before release; CI runs SAST, secret scanning and container scanning. No DAST.
items.next: Add DAST (ZAP baseline) against the sandbox gateway in CI.

items.title: Source code or escrow for critical applications; vulnerability-closure SLAs in contracts; vendor risk assessment for supply-chain risk; maintenance and support in contract
items.note: Open-source code is in hand; the supply-chain gate `vet` and hash-pinned installers cover third-party code; escrow and SLA clauses are contractual.
items.next: None for the software; the contract clauses are the entity's.

items.title: Secure by design / engineering / operations; least functionality (disable unneeded ports, services); application allow-listing on all assets
items.note: Kubernetes manifests run non-root with read-only root filesystems and dropped capabilities (enforced by Kyverno); compose services expose only declared ports; no host-level application allow-listing.
items.next: Document and test the exposed-port set per stage (the sandbox can assert it).

items.title: Hardened vetted hardware/software; default credentials replaced; non-default ports; port whitelisting; PowerShell/wscript restricted; host firewall to limit lateral movement
items.note: Pinned versions, scanned images and hardened manifests; Windows/PowerShell controls are the entity's.
items.next: Run docker-bench/kube-bench in CI and fail on regressions.

items.title: Change management in all third-party agreements; submit-plan-approve-implement-review-close; exceptions framework
items.note: Pull requests, CI, a build contract and `diffcheck` give a controlled change trail for this estate; exception handling and agreements are the entity's.
items.next: Release record with approver and impact note.

items.title: Regression testing, vulnerability assessment on each production release, VAPT on each major release; security requirements in BRDs; threat modelling and application security testing; OWASP ASVS; defence in depth
items.note: Unit tests and the sandbox journeys gate every release; threat modelling is documented per organ; independent VAPT per major release is the entity's engagement.
items.next: Attach a threat-model summary to each release.

items.title: Cyber audit by CERT-In empanelled auditors only (3-year limit then 2-year cooling-off); MD/CEO declaration; revalidation VAPT; audit management; automated compliance dashboard (MII, QRE)
items.note: Auditor appointment and the declaration are the entity's. `comply` and the evidence pack feed the dashboard.

items.title: Critical software must pass DAST, SAST, functional audit, VAPT per major release, firewall/WAF audit, SBOM, requirements traceability; all critical logs into the SOC
items.note: SAST, container scan and SBOM run in CI, and a traceability table maps requirements to journeys (doc 28). No DAST; independent functional audit/VAPT is an engagement.
items.next: Add DAST; feed every organ's logs to the SOC.

items.title: ISO 27001 certification covering primary, DR and near-DR sites, SOC and co-location (MII, QRE)
items.note: Certification is the entity's.

items.title: Follow the latest CIS Controls or equivalent (MII, QRE)
items.note: The compliance map cites CIS Controls v8; no CIS-benchmark evidence is collected.
items.next: Run CIS benchmarks for the container host and Kubernetes and store results in the pack.

items.title: Remote access policy and secure remote access for staff and third parties; trusted devices only; continuous monitoring of remote access
items.note: Cloud node access is via Tailscale (identity-based, Tailscale SSH) with a hash-pinned install; trusted-device checks and continuous remote-access monitoring are not implemented.
items.next: Tailnet ACL template + audit of remote sessions into the SOC.

items.title: Patch management: categorisation, test in identical non-production, replace EOL, virtual patching ≤6 months, High 1 week / Moderate 2 weeks / Low 1 month at both sites, quarterly compliance report to IT Committee
items.note: Versions are pinned and scanned; the KEV report names exploited vulnerabilities; there is no patch-SLA clock or quarterly compliance report.
items.next: Patch-age tracker with the 1-week/2-week/1-month limits and a quarterly report.

items.title: Continuous security monitoring and alerting; SOC services (own, market SOC, or third-party; small and self-cert on market SOC); SOC functional efficacy measured (Annexure-N) half-yearly; BAS/CART/decoy; MII 24×7 C-SOC
items.note: The AI-SOC triages gateway events 24×7 in software with ATT&CK/KEV enrichment, and the purple loop measures detection of known attack types. It is not a staffed SOC, does not cover endpoints/network beyond the optional Wazuh organ, and Annexure-N efficacy is not computed.
items.next: Compute Annexure-N efficacy indicators from the purple-loop results; add decoy/canary tokens.

items.title: Monitor IT-asset use and capacity; projections
items.note: See PR.DS (capacity).
items.next: As above.

items.title: Cyber audit and VAPT with Annexure-L scope; VAPT before commissioning new critical systems; revalidation; report COTS vulnerabilities to vendors/exchanges
items.note: Internal continuous testing exists (purple loop, range, scans); the independent VAPT is the entity's engagement.
items.next: Generate the Annexure-L scope sheet from the inventory.

items.title: Half-yearly red-team exercise by independent red/blue teams; CART; results to IT Committee and Board; lessons shared with SEBI within 3 months (MII, QRE)
items.note: The purple loop is an automated, AI-focused red/blue exercise with a gap backlog; it is not an independent human red team and does not cover the whole estate.
items.next: Extend scenarios beyond the AI path and produce the 3-month lessons-learned note automatically.

items.title: Quarterly threat hunting using threat intelligence, IOCs, IOAs (MII, QRE)
items.note: No hunting workflow; KEV/ATT&CK enrichment helps analysts but nothing runs hunts.
items.next: Scheduled hunts that run Sigma rules over the stored logs and file SOC cases.

items.title: CCMP aligned with CERT-In national CCMP, Board-approved; incident-response management plan, roles, SOPs; SEBI reporting SOP (Annexure-O)
items.note: An incident runbook and SOC case classes exist; the CCMP, its approval and the Annexure-O classification handling are the entity's.
items.next: Map SOC severities to the Annexure-O categories.

items.title: Awareness, training, skills, cyber playbooks, knowledge base of known adverse conditions
items.note: SOC rules and n8n workflow templates act as playbooks; people and training are the entity's.
items.next: Generate a playbook per SOC rule.

items.title: Collaborate with CERT-In's Cyber Swachhta Kendra; close alerts in time (MII, QRE)
items.note: Entity enrolment.

items.title: Report incidents to SEBI and CERT-In within 6 hours (mkt_incidents@sebi.gov.in), details on the SEBI portal within 24 hours, brokers/DPs also to exchange/depository; quarterly reports within 15 days of quarter end; share threat intelligence; RCA and forensic reports on request
items.note: Nothing tracks the 6-hour and 24-hour clocks, prepares the notification or the quarterly report, or maintains the contact list.
items.next: `./securax incident` (shared with RBI para 28/141): clock, templates for e-mail/portal fields, quarterly roll-up, TLP labelling.

items.title: IT Committee discusses response plans; stakeholder contact list; press release for high-impact attacks; notify affected customers; alternate-channel notification of transactions
items.note: Communications are the entity's.

items.title: Investigate alerts; collect and preserve incident data (logs, traffic, forensic images); analyse scope, cause and impact
items.note: Gateway audit lines and SOC cases are preserved; forensic imaging, memory capture and chain-of-custody are not provided.
items.next: Evidence-preservation step in `incident` (hash and seal the relevant logs).

items.title: Root-cause analysis, forensics, incident report, compromise assessment by a CERT-In empanelled auditor, impact analysis per Annexure-O
items.note: Forensics and the empanelled assessor are the entity's.

items.title: Update contingency plan, COOP, training and incident plans from lessons learnt (half-yearly for MII/QRE); Board approval of changes
items.note: Game-day and purple-loop reports produce lessons; plan updates and approval are the entity's.
items.next: Lessons-learnt register with owner and due date.

items.title: Scenario-based recovery plan; tests involving stakeholders; golden images of critical systems off-site (MII, QRE); spare hardware; protected images/backups; immutable or air-gapped backups; drills incl. ransomware with both PDC and DR hit
items.note: Etcd snapshot/restore and stage rebuild from the genome are drilled (game days). No golden images off-site, no immutable/air-gapped backup, no ransomware-on-both-sites drill.
items.next: Immutable off-site copy (object lock / offline disk) + a ransomware game day that destroys the live and local-backup copies.

items.title: Declare disaster within 30 minutes; RTO 2 hours and RPO 15 minutes; scenario-based resilience testing twice a year (MII, QRE: backup restore testing), stakeholders included, results to IT Committee, lessons to SEBI in 3 months
items.note: Restore time on the twin is seconds-to-minutes (12.5 s etcd restore), well inside 2 hours; but a 15-minute RPO needs near-continuous data capture and today's backups are periodic. Testing is available, not scheduled, and not reported to a committee.
items.next: Postgres WAL archiving for ≤15-minute RPO; schedule the twice-yearly drill; report generator for the IT Committee and SEBI.

items.title: Periodic drills to test response and recovery
items.note: Game days exist but are run on demand.
items.next: Schedule via `rhythm`; record attendance and outcomes.

items.title: Backup and recovery plan approved by IT Committee; data and server images backed up off-site; offline encrypted backups tested quarterly (MII, QRE)
items.note: `backup` writes owner-only archives that you copy off the machine yourself (3-2-1 is your step); no encryption, no offline copy, no quarterly test reminder.
items.next: Encrypted archives, automated off-site copy, quarterly restore test via `rhythm`.

items.title: Recovery plans discussed with IT Committee; stakeholder coordination and internal/external communication
items.note: Entity's governance and communications.

items.title: BCP-DR supports cyber-resilience objectives; learn from other REs' incidents; RTO met for interconnected systems; improve from drills
items.note: Restore from a cyber incident is rehearsed for the estate itself; interconnected systems of other parties are not.
items.next: Add the vendor/dependency outage scenario with stakeholder sign-off fields.

items.title: Anticipate new attack vectors via threat modelling; reduce attack surface; examine emerging threats; diverse OS and logging regimes; extra capacity; correlate data with ML
items.note: The purple loop and offline threat intelligence (ATT&CK, KEV) feed continuous improvement; fitness ratchets stop the attack surface (dependencies, `curl | sh`) growing; ML correlation is limited to the local triage model.
items.next: Quarterly threat-model review driven by ATT&CK coverage gaps from the purple loop.

items.title: Cloud adoption: hosted services on Tier-4-equivalent data centres, MeitY-empanelled CSP offerings audited by STQC-empanelled auditor, VAPT summaries available, copy of data in India if hosted abroad, data-in-use protection
items.note: The cloud stages (tree, canopy) can run on AWS, GCP or Azure; nothing checks that the chosen offering is MeitY-empanelled/STQC-audited, that the region is in India, or that a copy of data stays in India.
items.next: Provider/region guardrail in the lifecycle genome: refuse to wake a cloud stage outside an allow-list of India regions and CSPs the entity has verified; record the empanelment evidence.
